notes_md:
# Calif: "php2shell by Calif Research" — notes (collector-researchers)

- URL: https://calif.io/php2shell/ (linked from the calif.io homepage banner "Calif discovered php2shell"). Captured 2026-10-22T08:10:33Z, HTTP 200.
- Date: no machine-readable publish time; the comic timeline's last panel reads "Oct 21, 2026 and here we are...". Credits: "Research and writeup by Ryan Austin (@lcfr_hax) of Calif ... Poster and comic story by Michal Zalewski (@lcamtuf) of Calif."
- Framing: "two PHP remote vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) discovered by Calif, OpenAI and Wiz".

## Calif's timeline (verbatim from "An interesting timeline of events")
- "2026 — August 1 Calif discovered multiple different paths independently leading to RCE that resurfaced the 2024 issues and new trigger points."
- "2026 — August 5 Calif researcher Ryan Austin (@lcfr_hax) tweeted hash of one finding." (links https://x.com/lcfr_hax/status/2085031675382071483)
- "2026 — August 11 Calif reported the first bug to PHP and started coordinated disclosure process."
- "2026 — August 14 Calif shared an RCE PoC with PHP."
- "2026 — August 15 PHP confirmed that the RCE PoC worked as expected."
- "2026 — August 21 Calif reported the second bug to PHP."
- "2026 — October 21 Patched versions released."
- Comic panel 4: "July 30, 2026 Patch the Planet ... OpenAI invited us to join its Patch the Planet initiative ... Stefan connected us with Volker Dusch, who accepted our invitation."
- 2024 panel: "OSTIF and Quarkslab performed an audit of PHP and rediscovered the same OOM issue. However, exploitation was not proven, hence the bug was not fixed."

## AI angle
- "No special harness, or access to models that weren't generally available to everyone were used in the initial bug discovery." Austin: "I asked my LLM companion for help." Model is NOT named on this page (press says GPT-5.6 Sol).
- "We were not expecting to find anything critical - everyone and every lab had already done extensive AI assisted audits of this target."

## Exploit demos (not downloaded)
- Page embeds "Here is a demo video of the exploits running:" YouTube iframes: youtube-nocookie.com/embed/pfWZrdzvooc ("php2shell exploit demonstration") and /embed/cE4h79AWbT4 ("Exploiting Nginx with PHP-FPM"). Claims confirmed pre-auth RCE on WordPress 7.1.2, Drupal 11.4.3, Joomla 6.1.4, MediaWiki, Roundcube, Magento, phpMyAdmin, Nextcloud, Laravel, Symfony, WHMCS.
- Whether pfWZrdzvooc is the same video the PHP Foundation says Calif "mistakenly published" on Oct 20 is UNKNOWN. The page does not mention the leak or the deleted video at all.

## Contradictions
- Calif: discovery Aug 1; first report Aug 11. Fortune repeats Aug 1. PHP Foundation: Calif's audit began July 30, report Aug 11 (agrees).
- Calif homepage also links two archive.is snapshots (arHsF, spwCf), probably of WSJ/NYT coverage — not checked.

notes_md:
# CERT-EU Security Advisory 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP

- Stated "Release Date: 21-10-2026 15:20:18" (no timezone; CERT-EU is in Brussels, so probably CEST = 13:20Z, but that is not stated). History: v1.0 "Initial publication" and v1.1 "Updates with additional information", both 21/10/2026.
- Captured 2026-10-22T08:13:29Z.
- Key claims (verbatim):
  - "On 20 October 2026, the PHP project announced an upcoming security release addressing two critical vulnerabilities in PHP"
  - "The PHP team released the fixes today, 21 October 2026 at 13:30 UTC, in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35"
  - "Technical details are now being discussed publicly, and initial proofs of concept (PoCs) have begun to circulate. This raises the likelihood that attackers are already exploiting the vulnerabilities."
  - CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w), CVSS 9.2, OOM memory corruption; CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp), CVSS 9.2, stale global state.
  - "The PHP team considers mod_php the highest-risk setup."
- Exact advice: "CERT-EU advises organisations to patch affected assets immediately. Where that is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is applied and verified." Repeated under Recommendations as "isolating internet-facing resources from public networks".
- Temporary mitigations: memory_limit=-1 set via php_admin_value; low post_max_size; proxy-level request limits; cgroup memory limit (not RLIMIT_AS); session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restart workers; on 8.5 fatal_error_backtraces=0.
- Notes "rpms.remirepo.net ... will not have updates on release day".
- Its references include a Mastodon post by @GossiTheDog (cyberplace.social/@GossiTheDog/117474220875882526) and an X post by watchTowr (x.com/watchtowrcyber/status/2112611507749982605) as "public reports". Those are for the social/researcher collectors.
- Differs from CERT-FR on the release time: CERT-FR quotes PHP's pre-announcement of 16:00 Paris (14:00 UTC); CERT-EU says released 13:30 UTC.

- Page date 2026-10-21. "[Informācija publicēta 21.10.2026, plkst. 18:25]" = published 18:25 local (EEST, UTC+3), so 15:25Z. "[Informācija papildināta: 21.10.2026, plkst. 23:00]" = updated 23:00 local, so 20:00Z. The UTC conversion is ours.

A decision was made to temporarily restrict access to several state digital resources FROM ABROAD. Applied selectively. "Piekļuves ierobežojumi varētu būt spēkā līdz pirmdienai, 26. oktobrim". "Kopumā Latvijā identificēti aptuveni 6000 potenciāli ietekmētu resursu, no kuriem tikai daži simti ir valsts sektorā." - Credits: reporters lcfr-hax, sagitzadik-wiz, tomash-areion, amyb-oai; remediation developers arnaud-lb, iluuu1994, bukka, ndossche.
- Class: "PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors ... leaves the request memory in an invalid state ... lead to remote code execution (RCE)."
- SAPIs: mod_php unconditionally runs request shutdown even when startup failed: "This happens entirely before any application-specific code begins execution." FPM: "susceptible, though no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated for this SAPI." FrankenPHP "likely susceptible"; LSAPI "application-specific exploits being likely but unvalidated".
- Fix: removes longjmp() for OOM; "delayed, graceful soft OOM" at next VM safe point plus hard OOM via _exit() at a higher threshold.
- "Complete remote code execution was validated over HTTP against mod_php with default PHP input and memory limits".

## Contradiction
- The Foundation blog says RCE "was also confirmed on PHP-FPM through application-level code paths"; this GHSA says "no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated for this SAPI". (Possibly the blog conflates with the 109619 session path validated on FPM.)
- The reporter handle "tomash-areion" is not named in the Foundation's thanks list.

# NCSC (UK) alert: Critical security issue affecting PHP

- URL: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/news/critical-security-issue-affecting-php (NEWS TYPE: Alert)
- Stated: "PUBLISHED 21 October 2026". JSON-LD `datePublished` 2026-10-21, `dateModified` 2026-10-22. HTTP `last-modified: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 07:30:02 GMT`. The NCSC all-feed RSS lists it as `Wed, 21 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000`, but every item in that feed is 12:00, so the time is a placeholder and only the date counts.
- Captured 2026-10-22T08:09Z (capture 20261022T080903Z).
- CVEs named: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Links to GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp and GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w (php/php-src), and to NCSC-NL's php2shell repo (https://github.com/NCSC-NL/php2shell).

## Exact advice (priority actions, verbatim)
1. "Identify systems running PHP across your infrastructure, prioritising internet-facing systems. As all versions may be affected, do not limit discovery to outdated PHP versions..."
2. "Update to the latest version of PHP and continue to monitor for future updates."
3. "If you are unable to update to a version with the security update applied, the PHP Foundation have provided temporary mitigations."
4. "If you are unable to apply the temporary mitigations, or applying them would take too long, you should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated."
5. "If you are unable to update or disable the system immediately then you should assess the system for any evidence of compromise ... and look for backdoors installed by an attacker."
6. Monitor third-party vendors that bundle PHP; points to the NCSC-NL inventory.

## Oddities
- The BBC live page quotes the NCSC as saying "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated." That sentence is NOT on the page as captured at 08:09Z. The page carries the offline advice as step 4 (quoted above). ## Discovery (verbatim)

More recently, Trail of Bits has also been auditing PHP."
- Tools: "Earlier this year, we worked with Alpha-Omega to scan PHP with Anthropic's Claude Mythos ... OpenAI's Daybreak Red for validating reports and exploits".

## Leak (verbatim, section "Leak and disrupted disclosure")
- "The coordinated disclosure of these vulnerabilities worked well until 2 days ahead of the targeted release date."
- "On Tuesday, October 20th, at around 15:00 UTC, the two CVE IDs began circulating on online forums and social media. They came with a wrong release time and a wrong CVSS score of 10.0 (the actual score is 9.2). No technical details leaked." Pre-announcement moved to 19:30 UTC; release moved from Oct 22 14:00 UTC to Oct 21 14:00 UTC.
- "As a result of the leak and pre-announcement around 20:00 UTC, Calif, one of the security firms that had reported the issues, mistakenly published a video. It showed their proof of concept working against a number of targets and revealed a few additional, though limited, details about the vulnerabilities. Copies of the deleted video started circulating on social media soon after. The video contributed to accelerated development of various PoCs".
- "Mitigation advice we started providing to a few critical infrastructure providers around Oct 20th 23:00 UTC, may have leaked as well."
- "did not identify any functional exploits at the time of release/public disclosure."
